public_rationale: On April 10, 2026, Goldman Sachs reported technology-stock weakness alongside strong sector earnings and high returns on equity [e1]. That snapshot does not establish a sustained sector-wide collapse or connect one to the management and investment pattern described in the claim [e1]. Strong earnings at that date also cannot settle an open-ended forecast of future ruin [e1].
limitations: The cited assessment covers April 2026, not the full period through the October 28 evaluation date.
The packet does not establish sufficient continuation of the specified trajectory or a collapse caused by it.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The tech industry's current trajectory will lead it to ruin.

statement.excerpt: But that’s the thing, in many of my newsletters and podcasts, I’ve argued that the current trajectory of the tech industry will lead it to ruin.

our_interpretation: Ruin means a severe, sustained, sector-wide loss of economic strength and standing, not ordinary stock volatility or failure of individual companies.
The surrounding passage identifies the trajectory as shareholder-first management and major commitments to generative AI.
I retain current trajectory as a condition: the relevant management and investment pattern must persist long enough for its alleged consequences to be assessed.
The speaker supplies neither a deadline nor a required duration for that persistence.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that the described trajectory persisted and caused a broad, sustained collapse in the technology industry's economic strength and standing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive result establishing that the continued specified trajectory cannot produce the predicted ruin. A period of growth or a recovery alone cannot settle an unlimited forecast.
